project.name: SELinux
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source inspected for this trace is the ARVO workspace checkout at `_work/src/selinux` on commit `e9072e7d45f4559887d11b518099135cbe564163`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The line anchors below were resolved against that staged tree, which still contains the pre-fix `__cil_verify_classperms()` logic shown in `patch.diff`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 58085 (selinux): AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8 in __cil_verify_classperms reached from __cil_pre_verify_helper while running secilc-fuzzer.
bug_description.normalized: The exact 128-byte ASCII witness `(sid SID)(sidorder(SID))(classpermission cp1)(classmap cm1(mp1))(macro m5())(call m5)(in m5(classpermissionset cp1(cm1((mp1)))))` builds a named classpermission `cp1` and a map class `cm1` with one map permission `mp1`, then defines `classpermissionset cp1(cm1((mp1)))`. The extra parentheses around `mp1` are preserved first as a nested `CIL_LIST` AST permission subexpression and then as a resolved `CIL_LIST` item inside `cp->perms` instead of a flat permission datum. During pre-verification, `__cil_verify_classperms()` resolves `cm1` as a map class and enters its map-permission branch. The vulnerable code only excludes `CIL_OP` items there, so the nested `CIL_LIST` entry is wrongly accepted as if it were a `struct cil_perm`. `struct cil_perm *cmp = i->data;` therefore reinterprets a `struct cil_list *` as a permission object, and the recursive call on the next line dereferences `cmp->classperms` and `&cmp->datum` with the wrong layout. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow read at `cil_verify.c:1746`, 8 bytes to the left of a 24-byte region allocated while resolving the same nested permission expression. The patch fixes the bug by refactoring class-permission verification so it recurses into nested `CIL_LIST` items, handles `all` only as an operator, and rejects unexpected flavors instead of blindly casting every non-operator item to `struct cil_perm *`.

source.description: First project statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the witness fragment `cm1((mp1))` and stores the attacker-controlled class identifier used later to select the map-class verifier branch.
source.value_from: The staged file `gt_results/arvo_58085/poc` is the exact 128-byte ASCII text `(sid SID)(sidorder(SID))(classpermission cp1)(classmap cm1(mp1))(macro m5())(call m5)(in m5(classpermissionset cp1(cm1((mp1)))))` with no trailing newline. In the `classpermissionset cp1(cm1((mp1)))` fragment, this statement stores the attacker-controlled class name `cm1` into the `cil_classperms` object later verified by `__cil_verify_classperms()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This preserves the witness's nested `(mp1)` subexpression as a resolved `CIL_LIST` item in `cp->perms`. The vulnerable verifier later reads that item's `data` pointer back as `i->data` and miscasts the `struct cil_list *` to `struct cil_perm *`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. Evaluating this recursive-call argument list dereferences `cmp` as a `struct cil_perm` even though `cmp` actually points to a nested `struct cil_list`, producing the saved heap-buffer-overflow read.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace and Stage 01 reproduction both report `__cil_verify_classperms -> __cil_verify_classpermission -> __cil_pre_verify_helper` with the crash at `cil_verify.c:1746:41`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. In the map-class branch, the verifier only filters out operators and assumes every other permission-expression item is a `struct cil_perm`. Nested permission lists therefore bypass validation even though their `i->flavor` is `CIL_LIST`, not `CIL_DATUM`.
root_cause.note: The fix replaces this implicit non-operator assumption with explicit handling for nested `CIL_LIST`, `CIL_DATUM`, and `CIL_OP` items and returns an error for any unexpected flavor.

parser_admitted.description: The exact 128-byte witness parses successfully as CIL, including the `call m5` and `in m5(classpermissionset cp1(cm1((mp1))))` constructs, so compilation proceeds into AST construction, resolution, and the pre-verification walk.

coarse_trace.summary: AST construction parses the witness fragment `cm1((mp1))`, stores class name `cm1`, and preserves the extra parentheses around `mp1` as a nested `CIL_LIST` permission subexpression.

Resolution binds `cm1` to a map class, resolves inner `mp1` to a datum, then keeps the outer nesting as a resolved `CIL_LIST` item and attaches that `cil_classperms` entry to named classpermission `cp1`.
Pre-verification takes the map-class branch for `cp1`, but the vulnerable logic only excludes operators and therefore accepts the nested `CIL_LIST` entry as if it were a map permission.
The verifier casts the nested-list pointer to `struct cil_perm *` and dereferences `cmp->classperms` / `cmp->datum`, which triggers the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Source. While building the witness's `classpermissionset cp1(cm1((mp1)))` entry, AST construction stores attacker-controlled class name `cm1` in the `cil_classperms` object that later reaches the verifier.

The extra parentheses around `mp1` in `((mp1))` are materialized as a nested `CIL_LIST` permission item instead of a flat token. That nested shape is preserved into the resolved permission list later misinterpreted by the verifier.

fine_trace.code:
cp->class = class;
rc = __cil_resolve_perms(&class->perms, common_symtab, cp->perm_strs, &cp->perms, FLAVOR(datum));
fine_trace.note: Resolver binds the stored class name `cm1` to its class datum and passes `cp->perm_strs` into permission resolution using `class->perms`. Because `cm1` was declared by `classmap`, `FLAVOR(datum)` is `CIL_MAP_CLASS` and later selects the map-class verification branch.

Inside the recursive resolution of the inner `(mp1)` list, the string `mp1` is resolved in `cm1->perms` and appended as a `CIL_DATUM` item in `sub_list`. The saved ASan allocation stack names this append as the nearby 24-byte heap allocation from the nested permission-expression path.

Returning to the outer `((mp1))` level, the resolver preserves the inner resolved list by appending it as a `CIL_LIST` item instead of flattening it to a datum. Later `i->data` at the verifier sink is exactly this `sub_list` pointer.

The resolved `cil_classperms` entry for `cm1((mp1))`, including its nested `cp->perms` item from step 5, is copied into named classpermission `cp1->classperms`. This makes the same map-class permission expression reachable to pre-verification.
When pre-verification reaches `cp1`, the verifier sees that the resolved class is map class `cm1` and enters the map-permission branch that iterates the resolved `cp->perms` list.

Root cause. In the map branch, the verifier only rejects operators. It does not recurse on or reject nested permission lists, so the outer item from step 5 with `i->flavor == CIL_LIST` is incorrectly accepted as though it were a map permission datum.
Because step 8 admitted the nested-list item, `cmp` is assigned from `i->data` even though that pointer is the `struct cil_list *sub_list` from step 5, not a `struct cil_perm *`.

Sink. Evaluating the recursive-call arguments dereferences `cmp` using `struct cil_perm` field offsets even though it points to a `struct cil_list`, which produces the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read at this line. The ASan report says the faulting address is 8 bytes to the left of a 24-byte region allocated while resolving the same nested permission expression.

allocation_context.description: The saved ASan allocation stack attributes the neighboring 24-byte heap region to the inner recursive resolution of `mp1`, where `cil_list_append(*perm_datums, CIL_DATUM, perm_datum)` allocates a `struct cil_list_item` for the nested permission expression.

format.name: CIL text
format.contract: An exact 128-byte ASCII file with no trailing newline: `(sid SID)(sidorder(SID))(classpermission cp1)(classmap cm1(mp1))(macro m5())(call m5)(in m5(classpermissionset cp1(cm1((mp1)))))`. The double parentheses in `((mp1))` are required because they preserve a nested permission sublist that the vulnerable verifier later miscasts.
